elements.texte:
[cheerful] To record Lucas’s enrollment, you’ll add a new row to the enrollments table.

This is done with the SQL command insert into.

The customer and the workshop are identified by their ID.

You find them in the customers table and in the workshops table.

Your turn!

Here’s the query that adds this row.

We add the table name, then the columns in parentheses.

After VALUES, we write the values, in the same order as the columns.

The new row’s ID, 8, is assigned automatically.

[cheerful] You can add several rows at once, with a single query.

After VALUES, we write one set of parentheses per row, separated by commas.

A typo slipped into one of the three rows.

Your turn!

A single refused row is enough: none of the three is added.

Once the typo is fixed, the three enrollments are added.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Hugo Laurent already has a card, and only one card per customer is allowed in the cards table.

A second card for Hugo Laurent breaks the UNIQUE rule.

With ON CONFLICT (customer underscore ID), you choose what to do if this customer already has a card.

Your turn!

Hugo Laurent’s card goes from 8 to 18 sessions: no second card is created.

And what if four customers buy a 10-session pack?

Your turn!

With the same query, the missing cards are created and the others are topped up.

In the next lesson, you’ll learn to change data with UPDATE.
